context: A teacher explains formal Japanese registers to a student using examples
purpose: Teach: 市町村/にて/べく/かかわら/におきまして/某/いえる/１１月

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 今日は形式的な日本語、いわゆる「フォーマル体」についてお話しします。例えば「東京にて会議を行います」という表現、聞いたことありますか？
lines.en: Today, let's talk about formal Japanese, the so-called 'formal register.' For example, have you heard the expression 'A meeting will be held in Tokyo'?
lines.style: Teacher opens lesson with polite desumasu register and a concrete example.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ああ、駅のアナウンスとかで聞きます。「にて」は「で」のかしこまった言い方っていえると思います。
lines.en: Ah, I hear it in station announcements and such. You could say 'nite' is a formal way of saying 'de.'
lines.style: University student responds casually but respectfully, showing prior knowledge.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: その通りです。同じように「本日におきまして」も「今日において」のさらに丁寧な形といえるでしょう。役所や某大手企業の文書でよく見かけます。
lines.en: Exactly. Similarly, 'in today's session' can be called an even more polite form of 'on today.' You often see it in government offices or in documents from a certain major corporation.
lines.style: Teacher continues in polite desumasu, layering vocabulary explanation calmly.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 某って、名前を伏せるときの「某氏」とかの某ですか？なんかニュースっぽい響きですね。
lines.en: 'Bou' — like the 'bou' in 'a certain Mr. so-and-so' when you hide a name? It sounds kind of newsy.
lines.style: Student asks curiously in casual speech, connecting to media usage.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: ええ、まさにそれです。それから「年齢にかかわらず参加できます」のような「かかわらず」も覚えておきましょう。役所の案内文や、各市町村の広報でよく出てきます。
lines.en: Yes, exactly that. Also, please remember 'kakawarazu' as in 'anyone can join regardless of age.' It appears often in government notices and the public bulletins of each municipality.
lines.style: Teacher remains in patient polite register, giving practical real-world examples.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 市町村レベルの広報誌、確かに固い表現ばっかりですよね。先月、１１月の市報を見たら頭がクラクラしました。
lines.en: The bulletins at the municipal level really are full of stiff expressions. Last month, when I looked at the November city paper, my head was spinning.
lines.style: Student speaks casually with a touch of humor about real reading experience.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: ふふ、慣れですよ。最後にもう一つ、「目標を達成すべく努力する」の「べく」。論文や式辞で必ず出る形なので、しっかり身につけるべく頑張ってくださいね。
lines.en: Heh, it just takes getting used to. One last one — the 'beku' in 'striving in order to achieve a goal.' It always appears in papers and ceremonial speeches, so please work hard in order to master it firmly.
lines.style: Teacher closes warmly in polite desumasu, using the very form being taught.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど、自分で使ってお手本まで見せてくれたんですね。次のレポート、絶対この表現使ってみます！
lines.en: I see, you even used it yourself to show me as a model. I'll definitely try to use these expressions in my next report!
lines.style: Student responds with enthusiasm in casual-polite mixed university register.
